title: Reduce GPU runtime dependency footprint and implement fallback kernel strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket reduces the GPU runtime's binary and dependency surface by pruning unused CUTLASS variants, making Triton plugin loading optional, and adding a deterministic fallback kernel selection path for heterogenous GPU / driver environments. The goal is to shrink container image size, improve startup determinism on mixed customer fleets, and avoid runtime failures when a specific optimized kernel is unavailable. This addresses recurring incidents where missing kernel symbols or mismatched CUTLASS versions lead to degraded availability or emergency rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Container image size reduced by at least 12% compared to runtime-1.19 baseline without losing supported kernel variants
Kernel selection fallback correctly routes to verified alternative kernels (quantized or CPU) in >= 98% of simulated missing-kernel scenarios
Automated CI tests that cover kernel-absent and driver-mismatch permutations run in presubmit and return deterministic pass/fail
No regression in 99th percentile generation latency beyond 3% on the nightly benchmark suite for representative LLMs
Canary rollout completed with automatic rollback criteria defined and exercised on internal cluster
plan: Spike: binary dependency map - enumerate CUTLASS kernels currently built into runtime and their call sites (owners: Luca + infra)
Design: define a minimal kernel footprint policy and a safe-cut strategy for removing rarely-used variants
Implement: introduce a 'kernel-proxy' that resolves kernels at startup and falls back at call time to compatible alternatives or CPU stubs
CI: add matrix jobs that purposely omit certain kernel symbols and validate graceful fallback and correctness
Bench: run end-to-end perf suite against runtime-1.19 baseline and tune selection heuristics
Docs & Rollout: publish migration notes, canary plan, and ETA for dedicated clusters; coordinate with SRE and Support
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete - produced initial dependency map and found ~18% of CUTLASS kernels are unreferenced by our runtime call graph (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/2148)
2026-03-05: Decided to implement kernel-proxy rather than wholesale dynamic linking to keep startup deterministic; design doc submitted for review (confluence: /display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Proxy+Design)
2026-03-09: Prototype kernel-proxy committed; uses symbol table whitelist and a compact fallback registry. Added unit tests for registry lookups (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/2176)
2026-03-11: CI matrix job added that builds a trimmed image and runs smoke tests; uncovered two edge cases where quantized fallback produced precision shifts—investigating mitigations
2026-03-12: Bench run vs baseline (small LLM): median latency +0.4%, p99 +1.9% (within target). Image size improvement measured at 14% on dev image
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive pruning reduces image size and CI time but increases test surface for compatibility. We prefer a conservative removal list and rely on the proxy fallback to avoid customer impact. Longer term, we may split runtime into a tiny core + optional kernel bundles to let Dedicated/private customers choose variant sets. Coordinate with model-onboarding team to add telemetry tags when fallback occurs.
review_feedback: PM review (A. Singh): ensure rollout plan includes support playbook and rollback triggers
Security (J. Patel): requested a short audit of dynamic loading to ensure no new code-injection vectors
Design (R. Huang): suggested adding an opt-in env var to force 'strict mode' for internal canaries
